# Incident Report — MTA 2026-01-31 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Evidence reviewed
- `2026-01-31-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (51,181 frames, ~26.4 MB, capture duration 623.9s / ~10.4 min)
- No IDS/Suricata alert exports were present in the evidence directory — findings below are derived solely from packet analysis via tshark.

## Victim host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.1.21.58** (also seen briefly self-assigned as 169.254.227.202 before DHCP completed) |
| MAC | **00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2** (Intel NIC) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-ES9F3ML** |
| Domain/workgroup | WIN11OFFICE (Kerberos realm `win11office.com`) |
| Logged-in Windows user | **gwyatt** (observed as Kerberos CNameString in AS-REQ/TGS traffic from 10.1.21.58) |

## Malware family
**Not signature-confirmed.** No cleartext payload, PDB path, string, or hash match was observable — the actual payload was delivered entirely inside TLS 1.3 (with the destination further obscured by Encrypted Client Hello, SNI `cloudflare-ech.com`), so no file could be extracted or hashed from the capture.

Attribution is therefore **behavioral only**, based on the following TTP chain, consistent with a commodity malvertising-delivered stealer/loader:
1. Victim searches `www.google.com` (t=45.1s).
2. Immediately redirected through `hiyter.com` (t=45.3s) — a Cloudflare-fronted traffic-distribution/redirector hop.
3. Lands on a fake file-hosting page at `media.megafilehub4.lat` (t=45.8s), which loads `cdnjs.cloudflare.com` assets (fake "download" landing page).
4. Fetches a **16 MB payload over TLS** from `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` (t=48.3–70.7s, 19,722 packets, 16 MB down / 629 KB up on 10.1.21.58:54840↔104.21.46.67:443), with the real SNI hidden behind Cloudflare ECH.
5. Post-execution, the host performs a **JavaScript browser/device-fingerprinting handshake** with `whitepepper.su` (153.92.1.49) via cleartext HTTP `GET/POST /api/set_agent` — collecting WebGL renderer, canvas fingerprint, screen/hardware info, plugins, WebRTC/audio data, then POSTing it back (classic anti-analysis/bot-filtering gate, "ClickFix"-style TDS behavior).
6. This is followed by a tight polling loop against `whitepepper.su:443` (roughly one connection every 0.7–3s between t=94s and t=122s) — behaviorally consistent with a C2 check-in/tasking loop.
7. Additional short-lived TLS sessions to `whooptm.cyou`, `holiday-forever.cc`, and `communicationfirewall-security.cc` follow in the same t=90–132s window.
8. No further activity to any of these hosts occurs during the remaining ~8 minutes of the capture.

## Indicators of Compromise (all observed directly in traffic)

### DNS/domains resolved and queried by the victim
| Domain | Resolved IP(s) | Role (behavioral) |
|---|---|---|
| hiyter.com | 104.21.22.231, 172.67.207.145 | Redirector / TDS hop |
| media.megafilehub4.lat | 104.21.48.156, 172.67.154.67 | Fake file-hosting landing page |
| arch.filemegahab4.sbs | 104.21.46.67, 172.67.136.13 | Payload delivery (16 MB, TLS+ECH) |
| whooptm.cyou | 62.72.32.156 | Post-infection contact |
| whitepepper.su | 153.92.1.49 | Fingerprinting gate + repeated C2-style polling |
| holiday-forever.cc | 80.97.160.24 | Post-infection contact |
| communicationfirewall-security.cc | 104.21.9.36, 172.67.141.109 | Post-infection contact |

### C2 / malicious network endpoints (IP:port)
- 153.92.1.49:443 and 153.92.1.49:80 (whitepepper.su) — confirmed cleartext HTTP fingerprinting/beacon traffic, repeated polling
- 62.72.32.156:443 (whooptm.cyou)
- 80.97.160.24:443 (holiday-forever.cc)
- 104.21.9.36:443 (communicationfirewall-security.cc, Cloudflare-fronted)
- 104.21.46.67:443 (arch.filemegahab4.sbs, payload host, Cloudflare-fronted with ECH)
- 104.21.48.156:443 (media.megafilehub4.lat)
- 104.21.22.231:443 (hiyter.com)

### Malicious URLs (observed cleartext, from HTTP requests to whitepepper.su)
```
http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome
http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome&act=log
http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge
http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge&act=log
http://whitepepper.su/favicon.ico
```
Bot/victim ID observed in traffic: `3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C`, auth token: `842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b`

### Transferred files / hashes
**None recoverable.** All HTTP-visible object transfers (`connecttest.txt`, `favicon.ico`, the `set_agent` fingerprinting HTML/JS, a Google time-sync stub) are benign or fingerprinting artifacts, not the payload — exported via `tshark --export-objects http`. The actual 16 MB payload from `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` was transported entirely inside TLS 1.3, so no file name or SHA256 could be extracted from the capture.

## Notes / scope limits
- No lateral movement observed: SMB2/DCERPC traffic to 10.1.21.2 is limited to routine SAMR/LSARPC/DRSUAPI Active Directory operations, no file writes.
- No unusual destination ports were used — all suspicious traffic rode standard 443/80, blending with legitimate Windows/Google/Microsoft telemetry that dominates the rest of the capture.
- JA3 client hashes were extracted for the TLS sessions to whitepepper.su (`2800f914a7a4ba98aa9df62d316a460c`, `65303e4e36f3e94aa300b91e81cb6992`, `966876ab31aa46bd3378db27b35b8d56`) for reference/pivoting, but were not matched against any signature database (no internet lookups performed per instructions).
